purpose: Skeleton-first pelvis/sacrum audit. Preserve corroborated hip joint centres while separating sacral size from low-confidence os coxae geometry.

sacrum_length_crosscheck.interpretation: The current a003 sacral reference length is within the adult male dry-bone corridor and is not, by itself, evidence of a sacral length defect.

findings: The sacrum is a useful example of why the skeleton-first rebuild must not blindly replace every a003 dimension. Its ~103 mm reference span is compatible with independent male sacral-length data (~108 ±10 mm).

The bilateral hip bones remain low-confidence because the current representation is a single SI-to-pubic reference segment with the acetabulum stored separately as a joint marker; that stick cannot stand in for the full ilium/ischium/pubis geometry.

The fitted HJC remains provisionally retained because it is independently corroborated. Rebuilding the os coxae must therefore preserve the acetabular/HJC relationship rather than shifting the HJC to match the current mesh.
Canonical pelvis geometry needs explicit ASIS, AIIS, PSIS, ischial spine, ischial tuberosity, pubic symphysis, acetabular rim/centre and SI auricular-surface landmarks on each hip bone.
Pelvic width and muscular appearance should later be generated by bone geometry plus soft tissue; the current r95 crotch and surface breadth cannot be used as hard skeletal dimensions.
canonical_requirements: Store sacral promontory, S1 endplate/body, sacral apex, bilateral auricular surfaces and sacral width/curvature separately.
Store os coxae landmarks sufficient to represent ilium, ischium and pubis despite their adult fusion into one conventional bone per side.
Keep each adult os coxae as one bone in the 206 count; developmental subparts are landmark regions, not added adult bones.
Use explicit bilateral SI contact centres and a pubic-symphysis contact frame.
Retain HJC only if the rebuilt acetabular geometry continues to support it.
acceptance_tests: Sacral length/width/body dimensions fall inside multi-source adult corridors.
HJC lies inside the reconstructed acetabular envelope and retains independent anthropometric support.
Left/right os coxae are mirror-consistent but not artificially collapsed into one pelvis stick.
SI and pubic contacts are distinct and geometrically closed.
Hip 3-DOF and SI nutation tests are rerun after pelvis geometry changes.
